data.reason: Modem re-registered and shows OPERATIONAL since ~02:28 (modem-events.jsonl, modem-metrics.jsonl), but the firewall's WAN still cannot reach the ISP gateway (ping 198.51.100.1 100% loss) with a stale dhclient lease. Watchdog itself flagged reload at 02:30/02:40 but only recorded would_reload in observe mode. Reconfiguring the WAN interface / renewing the DHCP lease should re-establish the connection.

data.error: action must be one of: change_config, contact_provider, investigate_further, none, reboot_host, replace_hardware, restart_service

data.cause: The ISP link dropped at ~02:01 (modem lost sync, TFTP config-file failure, then the modem rebooted and re-registered as OPERATIONAL around 02:28), but the firewall's WAN interface still holds the pre-outage DHCP lease and was never reconfigured after the modem recovered, so traffic never reaches the ISP gateway.
evidence: ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 (ISP gateway): 100% packet loss; ping -c 3 -n 1.1.1.1: 100% packet loss, while 'arp -a' shows the gateway entry resolved on vtnet0 — L2 up, no IP connectivity
ifconfig vtnet0: UP,RUNNING,LOWER_UP with inet 198.51.100.27 — the WAN NIC itself is fine
cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0: lease predates the outage (renew not due until 2026/3/5), i.e. stale across the 02:01 drop and 02:28 modem re-registration

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl: 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 02:01:44, 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND' at 02:14:10, 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' at 02:28:21
/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl: NOT_SYNCHRONIZED at 02:06, OPERATIONAL by 02:29 and still OPERATIONAL at 02:40 — the provider link recovered
/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: watchdog in observe mode logged would_reload at 02:30 and 02:40 but changed nothing; state.json shows last_action reload with modem operational
data.recommendation: A wan_reload was requested and its preconditions were met: renewing the WAN DHCP lease now that the modem is OPERATIONAL should restore internet. The operator should also let the watchdog act (not merely observe) once the modem reports OPERATIONAL after settling, and ask the ISP to check the flaky cable segment (ranging timeouts, missing config file, rising uncorrected codewords) that triggered the outage.
